problem: Evaluate the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=9xy$ along the ellipse $C$ with equation ${x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}=16,$ traversed once in the counterclockwise direction.

activity_context.topic_title: Line Integrals of Scalar Functions Over Ellipses

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14057969/assets/570b00c901daedddc9fe05855e2df5fb2c24158320544b955bda651210d9f803.png)

Evaluate the line integral ${\int }_{C}16xy\,\text{d}s,$ where the curve $C$ is the quarter of the ellipse ${x}^{2}+9{y}^{2}=9$  traversed from the point $(0,1)$ to the point $(-3,0).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

Note that we can write the equation of our ellipse in the form

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{3}^{2}}+{y}^{2}=1.
$$

So, the curve $C$ is an ellipse centered at $O$ with horizontal and vertical semiaxes of $3$ and $1,$ respectively. Therefore, it can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le t\le \pi .
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{8{sin}^{2}⁡t+({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =\sqrt{1+8{sin}^{2}⁡t}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=16xy$, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =16\cdot 3\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡t=48\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}16xy\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }48\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot \sqrt{1+8{sin}^{2}⁡t}\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =48{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\sqrt{1+8{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

We can solve this using the substitution $u=1+8{sin}^{2}⁡t,$ $\text{d}u=16\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}48{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\sqrt{1+8{sin}^{2}⁡t}\,\text{d}t & =3{\int }_{9}^{1}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\cdot \frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2}{|}_{9}^{1} \\  & =2({1}^{3/2}-{9}^{3/2}) \\  & =2(1-27) \\  & =-52\end{aligned}
$$
